properties.name: Schema prose must not assert what the schema cannot hold, because the prose is what agents are told
properties.statement: reflow2 validates the schema's STRUCTURE and never its PROSE, and the prose is the discovery surface. tools/validate_schema.py states its own scope: the two hard rules are that every edge from/to endpoint is `*` or a declared node type, and that fulltext:true appears only on string properties, plus serde-level constraints on property type and resolution.strategy — and then, verbatim, "Everything else (extra keys like `description`) is accepted, matching serde's non-strict parse." So extraction_hint and description are free text no check ever reads. THE PART THAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN DOCUMENTATION HYGIENE: describe_schema serves extraction_hint VERBATIM to any agent asking what the vocabulary contains. Unvalidated prose is therefore not a comment — it is an instruction delivered to every agent that meets this schema, and a wrong one is wrong at scale, silently, forever. THE PROVEN INSTANCE, which is evidence rather than the point: schema/structure.yaml:108 and schema/verify.yaml:63 jointly assert, from both ends, a DEPENDS_ON relationship between Anchor and DriftEvent — "DriftEvents reference the Anchor they diverged from" and "References the Anchor it diverged from via DEPENDS_ON". That relationship has zero instances and no code path able to create one, because Anchor is a dead type superseded by Snapshot (see dec:anchor-retire-or-implement). BOTH HINTS PASS validate_schema.py CLEANLY, because it does not look at prose. An agent following either one creates a node nothing will read and believes it has anchored a build round. THE PRIOR ART, one level over: reflow's validate_workflow_files.py checked reference integrity inside its own definition files — "tool references point to existing tools", "template references point to existing templates", "next_step references point to valid steps" — with the stated benefit "prevents deployment of malformed workflows that would break Reflow". reflow2 has no equivalent for the vocabulary it serves. A MECHANICAL CHECK IS AVAILABLE, which is why this is a requirement rather than a wish: does every node type and edge type NAMED in a hint actually exist in the merged schema, and does every relationship a hint asserts have a corresponding edge type declared between those endpoints? Both are answerable without an LLM, from the schema alone, and both would have caught the Anchor case. What cannot be mechanised — whether a hint's advice is good — stays a human question and should not be pretended otherwise. THIS IS THE SAME FAMILY as req:defaults-do-not-assert, req:edge-defaults-do-not-assert and req:functional-vocabulary-computes, one layer up: those are data the schema asserts without warrant, this is PROSE the schema asserts without warrant — and it is the layer agents actually read. Found 2026-07-28 reviewing 98-reflow_feature_update.json. Anthony's word: capture it.
